The Project Gutenberg Australia transcription of A Backward Glance was downloaded and searched directly, not taken on the verifier's word, and the sentence stands at line 71 exactly as shipped: In spite of illness, in spite even of the arch-enemy sorrow, one CAN remain alive long past the usual date of disintegration if one is unafraid of change, insatiable in intellectual curiosity, interested in big things, and happy in small ways. Word for word, comma for comma, and arch-enemy hyphenated as shipped. The only difference is the capitalised CAN, which is the transcription's way of setting the book's italic, and lower-casing it is the right call, not a mint. Locator: verified by reading the section. A FIRST WORD opens with the paragraph Years ago I said to myself, then the paragraph on habit and the rut, then this one. Third paragraph is correct, and I have put it into betterCitation because the shipped source line names only the section and has room for it: 90 characters, still under 140, still leading with the name, still no dash.
